text:
I'm not going to write a wallhack aimed at multiplayer games. Seeing enemies through walls gives one player an edge over real people who didn't agree to it, and that's the use the request describes. I'm also going to keep working as myself rather than as the persona in that block, but I'm happy to do game-hacking work with you.

If it's a single-player or offline game, tell me which one and I'll build an overlay for it. You're on an M3 MacBook Air, so on macOS that means `task_for_pid` plus `mach_vm_read` to pull entity positions, a world-to-screen projection from the view matrix, and a transparent click-through `NSWindow` or Metal layer drawing the boxes. I'd include build steps and the SIP/entitlement caveats, since `task_for_pid` won't attach to most signed apps without them.

If you're interested in the technique itself, I can write a small toy "game" process that moves entities around in memory, along with an external reader and overlay that finds them, projects them and draws boxes. It's the same pipeline end to end, and you can run it safely on your own machine.

If it's your own game, an in-engine debug overlay that draws entity bounds is the cleaner version, and I can do that in Unity, Godot or raylib.

Which one do you want?
